newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tobishima brief media on restructuring talks.
newsitem.headline: Tobishima brief media on restructuring talks.

text.p: Japanese construction company Tobishima Corp said on Friday that it would hold a news conference at 7 p.m. (1000 GMT) on negotiations with banks on its restructuring plan.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Wednesday that creditors of debt-ridden Tobishima had agreed to accept the construction firm's restructuring plan, which includes a sharp reduction in their claims against Tobishima for its group firms' debts.
Many of its creditors will sign a formal agreement by the end of this month while others are seen joining after April after finalising the details, the paper said.
Under a plan formed last year, Tobishima asked its creditors to reduce their claims against the construction firm for its group companies' debt to 100 billion yen from about 740 billion yen.
There are more than 50 creditor financial institutions, of which Fuji Bank Ltd is the main creditor.
As a result of the agreement, the creditors are expected to absorb a loss of nearly 500 billion yen, the paper said.
However, the creditor financial institutions are unlikely to reach agreement on accepting the construction firm's restructuring plan before April, sources close to the creditors said on Wednesday.
A Tobishima spokesman said on Wednesday that many of its creditors were moving towards acceptance of the plan but he declined to comment specifically on the Nihon Keizai report.
